source_span.label: author theorem environment (unlabelled, carrying the in-card numbered equation eq:bounds_invL_Langevin at source line 609); statement at source lines 607-617, printed as Theorem 3.3 in the journal: under Assumptions ass:Poincare_nu and ass:Poincare_kappa the resolvent of the Langevin generator obeys the multline bound (eq:bounds_invL_Langevin) ||cL^{-1}|| <= (2 beta gamma)/(lambda_min(cLM) K_nu^2) ||Pi_1 cLFD Pi_1|| + (4 beta)/(gamma K_kappa^2) (3/4 + ||Pi_subplus cLham^2 Pi_0 (cLa_subplus0^* cLa_subplus0)^{-1}||^2 + gamma^2 ||Pi_2 cLFD Pi_1 cLham Pi_0 (cLa_subplus0^* cLa_subplus0)^{-1}||^2), where lambda_min(cLM) > 0 is the smallest eigenvalue of the symmetric positive definite matrix cLM = int nabla^2 U d kappa = beta int nabla U (tensor) nabla U d kappa

the author's own proof: applies Theorem thm:bounds_Linv and verifies Assumptions ass:A_inv, ass:macro_coercivity and ass:technical_ass -- the Poincare inequality in the momentum variable gives Assumption 2.2 with s = gamma K_kappa^2/beta; the adjoint rewrites partial_{p_i}^* = -partial_{p_i} + beta partial_{p_i} U and partial_{q_i}^* = -partial_{q_i} + beta partial_{q_i} V with the commutation rules produce the numbered identity eq:A^*A_Langevin (cLa_subplus0^* cLa_subplus0 = (1/beta) sum cLM_ij Pi_0 partial_{q_i}^* partial_{q_j} Pi_0); positive-definiteness of cLM follows from xi^T cLM xi = beta int |xi^T nabla U|^2 d kappa and the L^1 integrability of e^{-beta U}; the Poincare inequality for nu gives macroscopic coercivity with a = K_nu sqrt(lambda_min(cLM)/beta); for Assumption 2.6 the proof writes -Pi_1 cLFD Pi_1 = (1/beta) sum T_ij TildeT_ij with T_ij = partial_{p_i}^* Pi_0 partial_{p_j} bounded by an integration-by-parts estimate and TildeT_ij bounded as combinations of (nabla_q^* cLM nabla_q)^{-1/2} partial_{q_j}^* and adjoints, so cLs_11 is bounded; the remaining operator eq:op_for_Ass5 splits into the second term handled through the numbered action expressions eq:action_cLa2 and eq:Sij_Tij plus the boundedness of the second-derivative and drift blocks (in view of the regularization condition eq:regularization condition, via DMS15 Proposition 5 and ST18 Lemma A.4) and the first term handled through the explicit bounded operator scrT_i using the Assumption 3.2 moment bounds; the estimate eq:bounds_invL_Langevin finally follows by Theorem thm:bounds_Linv (source lines 621-711)

the regularization condition display eq:regularization condition inside Assumption ass:Poincare_nu: Delta V <= c_1 d + (c_2 beta/2)|nabla V|^2 and |nabla^2 V|^2 <= c_3^2 (d + |nabla V|^2), referenced by the counted proof at source line 698 (source lines 587-589)
